title: Top Monitors for Working From Home (2026)
summary: The Dell UltraSharp U3225QE is our top pick for a one-screen home office, with the Acer Vero B247Y G for tight budgets and the Asus ProArt PA279CRV for affordable 4K.
method: Picks come from PCWorld's home-office monitor guide (updated Jul 8, 2026), where the reviewer tests each monitor with a Datacolor Spyder X2 Ultra calibration tool. We did not find a second fresh, reliable guide for this topic, so every pick here rests on PCWorld alone. Prices are the ones PCWorld listed.
assumptions: Prices change often. PCWorld's 'price when reviewed' and its July deal prices are quoted below, so check the current price before buying. Specs are for the configurations PCWorld tested. PCWorld also covers a 6K Asus ProArt PA32QCV, a 52-inch Dell UltraSharp, a BenQ PD2730S for creatives and a Dell 2424T touchscreen, which we left out to keep this list focused.

products.name: Dell UltraSharp U3225QE
why: PCWorld names it the best home office monitor overall. The 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black panel gives sharp text, and a 120Hz refresh rate makes scrolling through documents and spreadsheets feel smoother than on typical 60Hz office screens.
It also works as a laptop dock: Thunderbolt 4 and USB-C with up to 140W of Power Delivery can fully power most laptops over one cable, plus extra USB-A and USB-C ports and Ethernet.
specs: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black panel, 120Hz with variable refresh rate
Thunderbolt 4, USB-C (up to 140W), Ethernet and a pop-out USB hub
Improved contrast of about 3000:1 for an IPS panel
PCWorld lists $949.99 when reviewed and $799.99 at Amazon in July; check the current price
cons: Contrast still trails VA and OLED panels
products.best_for: People who want one big, sharp screen that also docks a laptop
products.skip_if: You only need a basic screen for email and a budget under $200

products.name: Acer Vero B247Y G
why: PCWorld's best budget home office monitor. For about $150 it gets a 24-inch 1080p IPS panel, a 120Hz refresh rate with adaptive sync and a stand that adjusts for height, tilt, swivel and pivot.
Useful extras include a matte finish and high brightness against glare, a quick-release stand and a 1/4-inch tripod mount on top for a webcam or ring light, which PCWorld calls rare at this price.
specs: 24-inch 1080p IPS, 120Hz with adaptive sync
HDMI, DisplayPort and VGA inputs
Height, tilt, swivel and pivot stand with 1/4-inch tripod mount
PCWorld lists $154.99 when reviewed and $109.99 at Amazon in July; check the current price
cons: Only one HDMI and one DisplayPort
products.best_for: Budget buyers who want a comfortable, versatile main screen
products.skip_if: You want USB-C charging or a docking monitor

products.name: Asus ProArt PA278CFRV
why: PCWorld's best 1440p home office pick. The 27-inch 2560x1440 IPS panel covers about 97 percent of the DCI-P3 color gamut, which suits photographers and designers as well as everyday office work.
A USB-C port with 96W of Power Delivery can charge most laptops, and a built-in USB hub adds more ports. PCWorld says its 100Hz refresh rate easily beats rivals stuck at 60Hz.
specs: 27-inch 2560x1440 IPS, up to 100Hz with Adaptive Sync
USB-C with 96W Power Delivery plus USB-A and USB-C hub ports
Ergonomic stand with an ambient light sensor
PCWorld lists a $379 MSRP; check the current price
cons: Color accuracy does not beat peers
products.best_for: Home office workers who also edit photos or design
products.skip_if: You want the best contrast or true HDR
products.amazon_listing: ASUS ProArt Display 27” 1440P Professional Monitor (PA278CFRV) - IPS, QHD (2560 x 1440), P

products.name: Asus ProArt PA279CRV
why: PCWorld's best 4K home office monitor. The 27-inch 4K screen packs 163 pixels per inch and covers 100 percent of sRGB, 99 percent of DCI-P3 and 98 percent of AdobeRGB, a wide gamut for the money.
Connectivity is strong: USB-C with 96W Power Delivery, two DisplayPort 1.4 (one can daisy chain), two HDMI 2.0 and three USB-A ports, with a stand that adjusts for height, tilt, swivel and pivot.
specs: 27-inch 4K IPS at 60Hz
USB-C 96W, 2x DisplayPort 1.4, 2x HDMI 2.0, 3x USB-A
PCWorld lists a $469 MSRP, with $399 at Amazon in July; check the current price
cons: Only 60Hz, so motion is not smooth for games
products.best_for: Professionals and creators who want affordable 4K with accurate color
products.skip_if: You game on the same screen and want high refresh
products.amazon_listing: ASUS ProArt PA279CRV 27 Inch 4K UHD USB-C HDR Professional Monitor for Mac | Calman Verifi

products.name: Asus ProArt Display 5K PA27JCV
why: PCWorld's best 5K home office monitor. The 27-inch 5120x2880 panel works out to about 218 pixels per inch, and PCWorld says it is the least expensive 5K monitor available, at nearly half the price of Apple's 5K display.

It includes USB-C with 96W Power Delivery, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4 and a built-in KVM switch, so one screen can serve several computers. PCWorld measured up to 578 nits in SDR, bright enough for harsh room light.
specs: USB-C 96W, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, KVM switch
100 percent sRGB and DCI-P3, 91 percent AdobeRGB
PCWorld lists $799.99 when reviewed; Newegg showed $649 in July; check the current price
cons: Contrast is fine but not great
products.best_for: Anyone who reads small text all day or edits detailed photos
products.skip_if: You want high refresh for gaming
products.amazon_listing: ASUS ProArt PA27JCV 27 Inch 5K USB-C Professional Monitor for Mac | Calman Verified, Delta

products.name: BenQ RD280U
why: PCWorld's best monitor for coding. Its unusual 3:2 aspect ratio makes it much taller than a widescreen, so you see more lines of code at once and scroll less, on a 28-inch 3840x2560 panel that renders small fonts crisply.
Eye-comfort features include a MoonHalo ambient light and an automatic night mode, and a matte finish cuts glare. USB-C carries DisplayPort and 90W of Power Delivery for a connected laptop.
specs: USB-C with 90W Power Delivery
MoonHalo ambient light and night mode
PCWorld lists $599.99 when reviewed and $549.99 at Amazon in July; check the current price
pros: Tall screen fits more code or documents
products.best_for: Programmers and anyone working in long documents or spreadsheets
products.skip_if: You mainly watch video or play games
products.amazon_listing: BenQ RD280U 28.2” 4K 3840x2560 3:2 Programming Monitor, Eye-Care, Nano Matte Panel, Coding

products.name: Asus ZenScreen MB249C
why: PCWorld's best second monitor. It is a 24-inch portable screen that can sit next to your main display, clamp to the back of your desk, hang from a partition mount or go on a 100x100mm VESA arm.
A built-in kickstand and a stand that clips off make it easy to take on the road, and it runs from USB-C with up to 60W of Power Delivery or the included power adapter.
specs: 24-inch 1080p portable monitor
USB-C (up to 60W Power Delivery) or included adapter
Clamp stand, kickstand, partition mount and VESA 100x100
PCWorld lists $349 when reviewed; check the current price
cons: A bit pricey for what it offers
products.best_for: People who want a flexible second screen at home or on the go
products.skip_if: You want a high-resolution main monitor
products.amazon_listing: ASUS ZenScreen MB249C 24 Inch 1080p USB-C Portable Monitor | USB-C 60W, C-clamp Arm, Speak

tips.title: How to choose
items: Pick a size that fits your desk.
PCWorld calls 27 inches the goldilocks size for most people, while a 24-inch screen suits a shallow desk and 32-inch or ultrawide screens suit deep desks.
Choose USB-C if you use a laptop.
PCWorld recommends USB-C for most people because one cable carries video and charges the laptop. Check the Power Delivery wattage against your laptop.
PCWorld says 300 nits or more is ideal for a bright home office and that a home office monitor does not need HDR.
PCWorld says 1080p is more than adequate for most home office tasks, so you can save money unless you want sharper text.

faq: What is the best monitor for a home office?
PCWorld picks the Dell UltraSharp U3225QE, a 31.5-inch 4K monitor with a 120Hz refresh rate and strong USB-C docking.
What is the best cheap home office monitor?
PCWorld's budget pick is the Acer Vero B247Y G, a 24-inch 1080p screen with 120Hz and an adjustable stand, listed at $154.99 when reviewed.
Which monitor is best for coding?
PCWorld picks the BenQ RD280U for its tall 3:2 aspect ratio, which shows more lines of code on screen.
PCWorld picks the Dell 2424T, a 24-inch 1080p touchscreen with USB-C, but it calls it expensive for its size and resolution.
